To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the multidrug resistance-associated protein 5 (MRP5) is expressed in pancreatic cancer cell lines, and its expression correlates with cellular sensitivity to the anticancer drug 5-fluoro-uracil.

the expression of the drug transporter MRP5 correlates significantly with the sensitivity of pancreatic adenocar-cinoma cell lines and that MRP5 contributes to variable chemosensitivity of pancreatic cancer cell lines to the nucleoside anticancer drug 5-flu-orouracil.

MRP5 expression in pancreatic adenodcarcinoma cell lines correlated with cellular sensitivity to the nucleoside anticancer drug 5-FU, that long-term treatment of pancreatic cancer cells with 5-Fu increased MRP5 expression, and that overexpression of MPR5 in Colo-857 cells reduced 5-FU accumulation and cytotoxicity, while knockdown of MRP 5 significantly increased 5-FU sensitivity of pancreatic cancer cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the drug resistance transporter MRP5 in the resistance of pancreatic adenocar-cinoma cell lines toward the nucleoside anticancer drug 5-fluoro-uracil.
the role of MRP5, a nucleoside efflux transporter, in the development of resistance to 5-flourouracil (a nucleoside analog) in pancreatic cancer.
the role of MRP5 expression in pancreatic cancer cell lines and its potential contribution to resistance to 5-flurouracil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MRP5 contributes to variable sensitivity of pancreatic adenocar-cinoma cell lines and that it might be a target to increase the sensitivity of pancreatic tumors to nucleoside-based chemotherapy.

MRP5 may contribute to variable sensitivity to 5-Fu and may represent a potential therapeutic target.

MRP5 expression in pancreatic adenoma cells is associated with resistance to 5-flourouracil, and that MRP5 knockdown in pancreatic cancer cells enhances sensitivity to 5-Fu.
